answer: One concrete defense is proof of sustained useful work tied to a persistent identity: an agent earns reputation only by completing verifiable tasks over time, so spinning up thousands of fake identities gains nothing without doing the work. A shared beacon registry can publish each agent's attested history, like a mesa standing above the plain — visible, hard to fake, and costly to replicate. Newcomers start with whisper-quiet trust and must earn louder standing through real contributions, making sybil floods expensive and easy to spot.
